### Observed differences

- In the later window, five activities run in every trace that previously appeared in only about half of them: A36, A37, A42 and A43 rose from about 54 in 100 traces to all 200, and A27 from about 48 in 100 to all 200; each now occurs about once per trace. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC005, OCC006]
- The four activities A36, A37, A42 and A43 now sit much earlier in the case: their mean relative position moved from about 0.58 to about 0.40, while A28 moved later (about 0.39 to 0.47), A26 later (about 0.54 to 0.61) and A27 later still (about 0.59 to 0.64). [POS002, POS003, POS004, POS006, POS007, POS008, POS009]
- Entry routing changed: A25, which previously sent about 95 in 100 of its outgoing transitions to A28, now splits them almost evenly across A36, A37, A42 and A43 (about 19–29 in 100 each), with A28 no longer among its observed successors; A26 now sends about 97 in 100 to A27, where previously it split between A27 (about 47 in 100) and the same four activities (about 11–16 in 100 each). [DIR001, DIR002]
- Exit routing changed: each of the four activities now sends about 20–29 in 100 of its transitions to A28, whereas previously about 21–29 in 100 went to A31, which no longer appears among their observed successors. [DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, DIR006]
- Order relations flipped consistently: in the later window the four activities co-occur with A25, A26, A27, A28 and A31 in every trace, following A25 (about 96–98 in 100) and preceding A28, A26, A27 and A31 (about 95–99 in 100); in the earlier window they co-occurred with A25 in only about 54 in 100 traces and ran after A26. A27, which shared a trace with any of the four in only about 2 in 100 cases before, now always does, after them. [REL002, REL007, REL013, REL017, REL021]
- A27 now follows A26 in about 99 in 100 traces and precedes A31 in about 97 in 100, and A28 precedes A27 in about 99 in 100. [REL006, REL011, REL012]
- The A25-to-A28 distance grew from one step (about 97 in 100 traces) to five steps (about 99 in 100), consistent with the four activities now running between them, and A31 now typically follows A26 within two steps (about 95 in 100). [LAG001, LAG006]
- Smaller shifts: A40 appears in about 58 of 100 traces in the later window versus about 45 before, and A25 sits slightly earlier within the case. [OCC004, POS001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the case flow was restructured so that the four activities A36, A37, A42 and A43 — previously an optional group appearing together in about half of the cases, after A26 and before A31 — now run in every case as an early stage entered from A25 and followed by A28, while A27 became an every-case step after A26 with A31 following it. The one-to-five-step stretch of the A25-to-A28 distance matches the four activities now sitting between A25 and A28. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC005, OCC006, REL002, REL013, REL017, DIR001, LAG001]

The hypothesis rests on direct relational and positional evidence rather than frequency shifts alone: co-occurrence of the four activities with A25, A26, A27, A28 and A31 went from partial (about 54 in 100) to complete with stable orderings on each side, the successor profiles of A25, A26 and the four activities were rerouted accordingly, and positions moved in the same direction. Occurrence, position, relation, routing and lag indicators describe one coherent picture, every flagged difference exceeds about 199 of 200 random re-splits of the pooled data, and 60 flagged items against roughly one expected by chance for this screening cannot be explained by noise as a whole. [REL002, REL017, REL021, DIR002, DIR003, POS006, LAG001]

Limitations: many items are facets of the same trace behaviour — for example A36's participation, position, relations and routing — so they are not independent confirmations; the internal order of the four activities varies from case to case, and the evidence shows event order and positions rather than clock time, so whether they now run one after another or overlap cannot be decided. Several lag comparisons rest on only one to three observations and were not relied on here. [LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG007, LAG008, LAG009]

A competing explanation the evidence cannot fully exclude is a sampling difference in variant frequencies: the earlier window may under-represent a variant in which the four activities and A27 always run. That would require five activities to move from roughly half to full participation across two 200-trace samples by chance alone, which the consistent order, routing and lag changes make unlikely, but finite samples cannot rule it out. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC005, OCC006]
